title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.2 Incident response lifecycle: preparation
text: Incident response lifecycle: preparation. Preparation covers establishing the incident response capability, communications, and preventing incidents. It includes asset inventory, a baseline of normal behaviour, trained responders, and pre-approved containment actions. In an NDR deployment, preparation means knowing which entities are critical, what normal traffic looks like, and who can approve a block or isolation.

title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.3 Detection and analysis
text: Detection and analysis. Detection and analysis validates whether an event is an incident, determines its scope and impact, and preserves evidence. Analysts correlate multiple signals, establish the timeline, and identify affected hosts, accounts, and data. NIST notes that precursors and indicators may come from IDS/IPS, flow analysis, and anomaly detection; each alert needs triage, not automatic acceptance.

title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.3.3 Containment strategies
text: Containment strategies. Containment strategies are selected based on damage potential, evidence preservation, service availability, time and resources, and effectiveness. Short-term containment may isolate a host or block a source while preserving evidence; long-term containment applies a temporary fix and tighter monitoring before recovery. The chosen control must be reversible and documented with an expiry.

title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.3.4 Evidence gathering and handling
text: Evidence gathering and handling. Collect evidence in order of volatility, from CPU registers and memory to network state, running processes, disk, and archived media. For network incidents, capture flow records, packet captures, logs, and authentication events before changing the environment. Preserve chain of custody and hash evidence where required.

title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.4 Eradication and recovery
text: Eradication and recovery. Eradication removes the cause: malware, compromised accounts, and the exploited vulnerability. Recovery restores systems to normal operation with verification and heightened monitoring. Before restoring, confirm the entry path is closed and that persistence has been removed; after restoring, monitor for recurrence.

title: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.5 Post-incident activity
text: Post-incident activity. Post-incident activity captures lessons learned, metrics, and evidence retention. It answers what happened, how well the response performed, and what changes prevent recurrence. Track time to detect, time to contain, and the controls that failed.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 GV Govern
text: Govern. Govern sets risk management strategy, roles, and policy. It establishes the risk tolerance that determines when a detection becomes an incident and which response actions are pre-approved. Without governance, containment decisions are inconsistent between shifts.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 ID Identify
text: Identify. Identify covers asset management, risk assessment, and improvement. For NDR it is the inventory of entities, their criticality, and expected behaviour, which is the baseline that makes an anomaly meaningful.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 PR Protect
text: Protect. Protect covers identity management, access control, data security, platform security, and network segregation. Network controls such as boundary protection and segmentation reduce the blast radius of an intrusion and give containment points that already exist.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 DE Detect
text: Detect. Detect covers continuous monitoring, adverse event analysis, and detection process improvement. NDR contributes network-level monitoring and anomaly analysis; detections must be correlated and validated before response.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 RS Respond
text: Respond. Respond covers incident management, analysis, mitigation, and reporting. Response actions should be scoped, logged, communicated, and reversible where possible. Containment must be proportionate to the confidence and severity of the detection.

title: NIST CSF 2.0 RC Recover
text: Recover. Recover covers recovery planning, execution, and communication. Restoration follows eradication, with verification against the baseline and heightened monitoring for recurrence.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 IR-4 Incident handling
text: Incident handling. IR-4 requires an incident handling capability covering preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, and user response. The organisation coordinates with stakeholders, incorporates lessons learned, and protects incident information. Automated response actions must remain within the approved authority described by the plan.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 IR-5 Incident monitoring
text: Incident monitoring. IR-5 requires tracking and documenting incidents, including the status, the affected assets, and the response actions taken. An NDR console should preserve the detection-to-incident linkage and the action history for review.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 AU-6 Audit record review, analysis, and reporting
text: Audit record review, analysis, and reporting. AU-6 requires reviewing and analysing audit records for indications of inappropriate activity, reporting findings, and adjusting audit levels when needed. Network flow and detection records are part of that evidence set.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 SI-4 System monitoring
text: System monitoring. SI-4 requires monitoring the system to detect attacks, indicators of compromise, and unauthorized local, network, and remote connections. Monitoring includes inbound and outbound traffic, and the results must be analysed and escalated.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 SC-7 Boundary protection
text: Boundary protection. SC-7 requires monitoring and controlling communications at external and key internal boundaries, including denying traffic by default and restricting the flow of information. Edge blocks and rate limits used for containment belong to this control.

title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 SC-5 Denial-of-service protection
text: Denial-of-service protection. SC-5 requires protecting against or limiting the effects of denial-of-service incidents, including bandwidth exhaustion and resource depletion. Controls include rate limiting, traffic filtering, and upstream scrubbing.
